correctness.rationale: The proof constructs a generating character from a nontrivial socle character; ideal orthogonality gives the exact shell sum and all eigenvalue cases with unambiguous signs/normalization. Every valuation multiplicity and q=2 exception follows from a finite geometric derivative identity and (q-1)j=1. The universal proof covers k=1, arbitrary commutative finite chain rings, all residue field orders. The standalone exact cyclotomic and noncyclic chain-ring computations check representative cases, trace, rank, inertia, and q=4 characteristic-two nonexception. No finite sample is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Actual searches and a theorem-level comparison found no directly covering spectrum of the nonseparable set {(x,y):xy=0} on R^2 for every chain ring. The strongest inspected 2016 paper treats shell unions on the one-dimensional ring and separable gcd-graph tensor families; its techniques suggest the answer may be deducible, but its published statements neither assert the nonseparable class-specific rank nor resolve the q=2 cancellation. An 2008 finite-field restriction theorem and a 2010 quadratic-sum evaluation algorithm address different statements. Novelty is assessed only under bounded access, with a documented serious stronger-coverage risk.
residual_risks: An earlier association-scheme or nonseparable gcd-graph Fourier formula might specialize to the present spectrum; full historical coverage of that broader literature was not established.
Suntornpoch–Meemark 2016 provides a close general shell-spectral framework; although the nonseparable product-zero rank is not directly stated, it could be an implicit relatively short consequence.
No independent scholarly validation or outside expert review is claimed.
